item: the leftover-copy scan and its removal read one folder through one no-follow handle (R692 follow-up)
summary: BEFORE (R686, #1963): the scan for unencrypted volume copies an interrupted import left read the folder by path and probed each candidate by path, and the removal scanned again by path and only then opened its no-follow folder handle, so a folder swapped between the check and the open could turn the removal onto another folder holding the same vol-NNNNN.ooenc.plain names; a listed name in another letter case was not treated as listed, and the name pattern's $ let a trailing newline through. NOW: one pure function decides from the manifest's text and the folder's own listing (no path is built from a manifest name); on POSIX the manifest and the listing are read through the same no-follow folder handle the removal unlinks through, so what is checked is what is removed; listed names compare case-folded; the pattern is anchored with \A and \Z. Windows keeps one path read and one listing. Two tests, both red on the R686 code. Fewer CodeQL path sinks on the scan (each candidate probe is gone). Release line: none (a hardening of the R686 removal; no visible change).
